title: Add an opt-in stride-window tracking term to the experimental yaw-gated reward
summary: locomotion.task_v4_yaw_gate gains stride_tracking_weight and stride_window_controls (default 60, one schedule period). The term applies v4's linear and yaw tracking kernels to the mean displacement velocity over the stride window on moving commands, so it pays progress kept over a stride instead of a burst within it, and peaks at the commanded speed. v4's rule that the fall cost reach ten times the tracking ceiling now includes the term, so a weight above 1/3 needs a higher termination_weight. Scored on synthetic controls, weight 0.3 widens the reward gap between full and half commanded speed from 0.70 to 0.77 and weight 1 to 0.95; on nine stored replays it keeps the ranking of turners. The default 0 adds nothing; native runs remain the acceptance evidence.
next: Train the turn-heavy bonus-and-floor configuration on the surrogate with stride weight 0.3, and with weight 1 and termination weight 30, for 2000 updates on seed 20260917, and compare the probes and the heading drift with the run without the term.
reason: An opt-in option of an experimental task with surrogate design evidence changes no native result, gate or default reward.
